notes: Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue's row-letter convention: rows f-j (the top half of the photo, labelled j..f) are bank 'b', so holes look like '10b.g'.
Rail hole numbers (tp.2, tn.4, tp.6, tn.13, tn.26) are approximate positions read from the image; any hole in the same rail is equivalent.

In the photo the LED's bent (longer) leg is on column 22 and goes to pin 9 via the blue wire, so it is treated as the anode. The 220 ohm resistor sits on the cathode side (column 23 to column 26 to GND rail), which is electrically equivalent to the schematic's series arrangement.

The photoresistor goes from 5V (column 6, fed from the + rail) to column 10, which is the A0 node. The 10k resistor goes from column 10 to column 13, which is tied to GND. This forms the voltage divider.
The text says 'analog input 2' in the circuit caption, but the text and image both wire the sensor to A0, so A0 is used.
The Arduino GND wire uses GND.1; any Uno GND pin would work.
The 10k resistor value is written as 10000 and the 220 as 220 (ohms).
